seoTitle: Network Graph Visualizer: Force-Directed Layout Online
metaDescription: Paste an edge list and nodes arrange themselves by attraction and repulsion. Components get colours, size shows degree. Free SVG.
intro: Draws a network from pairs of connected names. A force simulation places connected nodes close and unconnected ones apart; a table lists degrees.
why:
Edge lists come from exports of links, emails, dependencies and social data. Seeing them as a graph shows clusters, bridges and isolated groups quickly.

The layout is a Fruchterman-Reingold style simulation with a fixed seed, so the same input draws the same picture, and you can change the seed for another arrangement. Direction and repeated edges are ignored. Beyond a few hundred nodes any force layout becomes a hairball; filter the list first.
howTo: Paste one connection per line: a,b or a -> b.
Turn labels on or off, change the seed for another layout.
Read the degree table for the most connected nodes.

faq.a: No, direction is ignored in the picture.
Each connected component has its own colour.

faq.q: Why do two runs look different with another seed?
faq.a: The simulation starts from a different random start; both layouts show the same graph.
